content.headline: Combination of Lapatinib and Fractionated Radiation Therapy for Dogs with Transitional Cell Carcinoma
content.tagline: Help us study canine bladder translational cell carcinoma.
content.description: This study is for dogs that have bladder cancer called transitional cell carcinoma (TCC). The goal is to find out if using radiation therapy together with a pill called lapatinib is safe and well‑tolerated by dogs. Researchers will watch closely for side effects and see how dogs respond to the treatment over about 4 months.
content.requirements:
1. Daily oral lapatinib and a non‑steroidal anti‑inflammatory drug (NSAID) throughout the study
  2. 15 daily radiation treatments, which require anesthesia each time, within the first 7 days of starting the pills
  3. Monthly recheck visits for 3 months after radiation for exams and blood tests
  4. Urinary ultrasounds to measure the tumor before the study starts and at the end
  5. All study visits must take place at Colorado State University (CSU) Veterinary Health Systems facilities (VHS)
content.who_can_participate:
Dogs may be able to join if they:

  1. Have a biopsy‑confirmed diagnosis of bladder TCC
  2. Can safely receive an NSAID
  3. Are healthy enough to undergo daily anesthesia for radiation treatment
  4. Have not had radiation in the last 6 weeks or chemotherapy in the last 2 weeks
  5. Can come to CSU VHS facilities for all study visits
content.benefits_and_risks:
Benefits

  1. High quality care for your pet
  2. The study covers the cost of:
  3. Lapatinib
  4. Recheck exams
  5. Bloodwork during the study
  6. $3,000 toward radiation therapy, which is provided at a reduced cost
  7. Urinary ultrasounds at the beginning and end of the study
  8. Sedation for ultrasounds if needed
  9. Some funds are available to help pay for treatment of side effects caused by the study

Risks

  1. Possible side effects from radiation therapy, lapatinib, or NSAIDs
  2. Risks related to repeated anesthesia
  3. The treatment may or may not help your dog’s cancer
content.time_commitment:
Study course: 4 months.
15 consecutive days of radiation therapy within the first 7 days of starting study drugs. Monthly rechecks for 3 months after finishing radiation therapy. Study drugs daily over the entire 4-month course of the study.
content.compensation:
The study covers the cost of: Lapatinib, recheck exams, bloodwork during the study, $3,000 toward radiation therapy, urinary ultrasounds at the beginning and end of the study, sedation for ultrasounds if needed.
Some funds are available to help pay for treatment of side effects caused by the study.
content.responsibilities:
1. Pay for the initial exam and all tests needed to diagnose the bladder tumor (including bladder scope and biopsy)
  2. Pay for the NSAID medication during the study
  3. Bring your dog to all scheduled appointments
  4. Give your dog oral medications every day
  5. Keep a written log of medications and any side effects you notice
